# Frontier-scaling findings — does classical-irreproducibility widen with scale?

*Generated by `frontier_scaling.py` (`cli.py run frontier`). The original H0 curve used the fixed
univariate encoder (idle qubits -> g declines). Here we push the **fully-informed** encoding (first
n columns of the rich realized-measure pool; P=19 >= n, so NO idle qubits) to the **n=16 exact
sparse frontier** and ask the one honest, striking question still open at simulable scale: does the
geometric difference g(ESN_n || CHIMERA_n) — how badly a matched classical reservoir fails to
reproduce the quantum kernel — keep GROWING with n? (This is a statement about classical
IRREPRODUCIBILITY, necessary-not-sufficient for beyond-frontier advantage — NOT an advantage claim.)*

## Results (kernel N_sub=400; dense engine n<=12, exact sparse expm_multiply n>=14)

| n | #feat | g(ESN‖CHIMERA) | g_control | g/control | D_eff | rank |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8  | 36  | 93.59 | 12.60 | 7.4 | 1.86 | 36 |
| 10 | 55  | 92.05 | 10.64 | 8.7 | 3.18 | 55 |
| 12 | 78  | 59.51 | 9.04  | 6.6 | 3.30 | 78 |
| 14 | 105 | 41.59 | 6.52  | 6.4 | 3.43 | 101 |
| 16 | 136 | 42.42 | 5.98  | 7.1 | 3.71 | 119 |

Spearman ρ(n, g) = **−0.90**;  ρ(n, g/control) = **−0.60**.

## Verdict — honest negative (with an instructive nuance)

- **g does NOT grow to the frontier — it declines/saturates** (93.6 → 42.4; ρ=−0.90), even under
  fully-informed encoding. The ratio g/control stays roughly flat (~7×): the quantum kernel remains
  several times harder to reproduce than the classical-vs-classical control, but **that gap does not
  widen with scale**.
- **Instructive nuance:** D_eff (1.86 → 3.71) and numerical rank (36 → 119) DO grow with n — the
  quantum kernel becomes genuinely higher-dimensional. But a *matched-size classical ESN keeps pace*
  in reproducing it, so irreproducibility (g) does not increase. Higher dimension ≠ harder to
  replicate.

**Implication.** The hoped-for "the could-matter gap widens with scale" pointer toward beyond-
frontier advantage is **not supported** in the testable range (n ≤ 16). Combined with the capacity
result (`information_capacity.py`: the quantum reservoir is not even more expressive at matched
scale), this closes the last simulable-scale route to a defensible advantage signal. The beyond-
frontier question (50–256 qubits on real hardware) remains genuinely open but is now *less*
encouraged by the trend within reach — reported honestly, without overclaiming in either direction.
